newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock fund flows drop in December.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock fund flows drop in December.

text.p: U.S. mutual funds suffered a decline in cash inflows this month amid volatility in stocks and as investors sought to duck tax liabilities.

"We're down quite a bit from last month because of market volatility," said Rowena Itchon, a spokeswoman at T. Rowe Price Associates Inc. "Earlier in December, we saw some serious downdrafts in the market."

The Dow Jones industrial average lost a total of 217 points during the first two weeks of December, then added nearly 260 points the following two weeks. Investors often sell stocks for tax purposes in the closing weeks of the year.
Fund companies said, however, that investors were still big buyers of large-capitalization funds, such as equity income and blue chips.

Carl Wittnebert at Mutual Funds Trim Tabs, said the fund tracking firm expected that inflows into U.S. equity funds would likely end at about $9.5 billion for December vs. $13.2 billion in November. The November figure excludes international and global equity funds.
Earlier on Monday, the Investment Company Institute, a trade group, reported that net new cash flow into mutual funds totalled $33.60 billion in November, compared with $34.52 billion in October.
Net flows into stock funds increased to $17.11 billion, from $13.55 billion in October.

Vanguard Group, which has $240 billion under management, has suffered a decline so far this month. Aggregate inflows through Dec. 27 totalled about $1.6 billion vs. $2.5 billion in November, according to spokesman John Woerth.
Part of the drop was due to Vanguard's advice that investors hold off on purchases until funds made their dividend and capital gains distributions for tax purposes. He also cited a weak market.
"There's rising concern about the level of the market, and the volatility earlier in the month," Woerth said.

Vanguard's equity funds experienced a drop to $1 billion from $1.5 billion; money market funds fell to $520 million from $625 million; and bond funds slumped to $105 million from $310 million, Woerth said.
Fidelity Investments said it estimated cash flows into its domestic equity funds will turn flat after more than a $1 billion inflow in November.
T. Rowe Price said the company was still seeing strength in large-capitalization funds, such as its equity income, growth and income and blue chip funds.
